title: Web-Integrated AI System for Bone Cancer Prediction
abstract: Bone cancer detection from X-ray images is challenging due to subtle tumor characteristics, radiologist fatigue, and limited access to specialized expertise, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Early and accurate diagnosis is critical for improving patient outcomes. However, conventional methods rely heavily on manual interpretation, leading to delays and variability. This study proposes a web-integrated AI system for automated bone cancer prediction using deep learning. The system employs the EfficientNet-B0 architecture with transfer learning to classify bone X-ray images as normal or cancerous, supported by preprocessing, data augmentation, and class-weighting techniques to address data scarcity and class imbalance. The trained model is deployed as a user-friendly web application enabling X-ray upload, report generation, scan history management, and interaction through an integrated AI chatbot. The proposed system aims to provide an efficient, interpretable, and clinically supportive diagnostic tool for early bone cancer detection.

title: QuATON: Quantization Aware Training of Optical Neurons
abstract: Optical processors, built with "optical neurons," can perform large-scale high-dimensional linear operations at the speed of light. With the current advances in micro-fabrication, such optical processors can now be 3D-fabricated, but at limited precision, eventually leading to a model mismatch due to quantized optical weights. To address this issue, we propose a quantization-aware training framework. Our approach accounts for physical constraints during the training process, leading to robust designs. We numerically demonstrate that our approach can design state-of-the-art optical processors using diffractive networks for multiple tasks despite quantized learnable parameters. We thus lay the foundation upon which improved optical processors may be 3D-fabricated in the future.

title: Wings of Perception: Investigating Customer Sentiments in Indian Aviation Sector
abstract: India's aviation sector, a key contributor to the nation's economy, has experienced rapid growth, supporting nearly 7.5 million jobs and contributing approximately $30 billion annually to the GDP (Gross Domestic Product). The growth, driven by increased demand for air travel and government incentives, has resulted in more competition among carriers. In the competitive market, it is necessary to understand customer preferences to enhance the quality of service and maintain a competitive edge. The dissemination of customer opinions on social media and review platforms offers airlines the opportunity to access passenger views. However, extracting useful information from this unstructured data is challenging. Previous studies had not accounted for variables such as seasonal fluctuation in opinion and the impact of specific service features on customer satisfaction. This study fills the gaps by employing sentiment analysis tools, including TextBlob and VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary for Sentiment Reasoning), to analyse customer opinions from platforms like X, Skytrax, and TripAdvisor. The study process involves data collection through automated web scraping tools, followed by data cleaning and text analysis to tag sentiments and identify variables influencing customer emotions. Key findings indicate that carriers like IndiGo and Vistara are highly rated by customers for punctuality, service quality, and operational consistency. Conversely, Air India and SpiceJet are faulted for delays and inefficiency. Seasonal patterns further indicate that negative sentiments are greater during peak travel seasons. The study highlights the importance of customer-centric initiatives, operational efficiency, and advanced analytics to boost brand loyalty in a highly competitive market.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Financial Crime Prevention: Translating Machine Learning Outputs into Regulatory and Compliance Decision-Making
abstract: Financial institutions increasingly rely on machine learning systems to detect fraudulent activities and prevent financial crime across complex transactional environments. Models like these are exemplified by their remarkable prediction accuracy, but at the same time, their lack of interpretability leads to considerable problems in terms of compliance with regulations, auditing, and operational trust. In the case of financial transactions that carry a high level of risk, regulators and compliance professionals want not just precise risk forecasts but also the reasoning behind the decisions to be open and understandable. The presented research introduces a regulatory-compliant explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework that connects machine learning results and financial crime decision-making processes. The framework does not innovate but rather focuses on converting risk scores and explainability outputs of predictive models into interpretable decision artifacts that can be easily reviewed for compliance, supervisory oversight, and human-in-the-loop validation. The proposed methodology combines explainability mechanisms with governance-oriented design principles, allowing for consistent justification of flagged transactions, enhanced audit trails, and increased accountability in automated systems for financial crimes detection and prevention. Case study illustrations demonstrate how explainable AI can support escalation, investigation, and reporting decisions in fraud and anti-money laundering contexts. The findings highlight the role of explainable AI as a critical enabler for aligning machine learning innovation with regulatory expectations, contributing to more transparent, trustworthy, and responsible financial crime prevention systems.

title: Latency Optimization in Long-Context GPT-5 Dialogues Using Memory-Block Compression and Controlled Context Refresh
abstract: This work investigates the problem of response latency escalation in long, multi-turn interactions with large language models (LLMs), such as GPT-5. As conversational history grows, transformer-based models repeatedly attend to an expanding context window, leading to significant increases in inference time and degraded user experience. The paper proposes a prompt-level optimization technique called the Memory-Block Protocol (MBP). MBP segments extended conversations into fixed-size blocks and replaces raw dialogue with compact semantic summaries, persistent state information, and a task ledger. By periodically refreshing the active context while preserving conversational continuity, the protocol bounds prompt growth and stabilizes response latency without requiring model retraining, architectural modification, or external memory infrastructure. An evaluation framework is presented to compare raw long-context conversations with MBP-optimized conversations across reasoning and technical tasks. The results indicate that MBP maintains semantic coherence while significantly improving responsiveness in long conversational sessions. The approach is model-agnostic and immediately applicable to real-world LLM usage in research, education, and professional workflows.

title: Satellite–Meteorological Data Fusion for Enhancing Short-Time Solar Irradiance Prediction
abstract: Adequate prediction of short-term solar irradiance is necessary to have a reliable contribution of solar energy to power grids, but it is not an easy task since the atmosphere varies rapidly and is mainly influenced by clouds, aerosols, and local weather conditions (Perez et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2018). This paper introduces a satellite-meteorological data fusion system, which is created to improve the short-term prediction of solar irradiance at high time resolution. The suggested solution will combine the geostationary satellite measurements, such as optical properties of the clouds and radiative flux estimates, with ground measurements and reanalysis of meteorological variables, such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and surface pressure (Schroedter-Homscheidt et al., 2016; Ineichen, 2014). The hybrid model attains data fusion, which involves the use of physical radiative relations alongside data-driven learning algorithms to obtain both the large-scale atmospheric patterns and the local variability (Voyant et al., 2017; Haupt et al., 2018).

title: ECLIPSE: An Evolutionary Computation Library for Instrumentation Prototyping in Scientific Engineering
abstract: Designing scientific instrumentation often requires exploring large, highly constrained design spaces using computationally expensive physics simulations. These simulators pose substantial challenges for integrating evolutionary computation (EC) into scientific design workflows, as they are optimized for accuracy and ease of use rather than throughput. We present ECLIPSE, an evolutionary computation framework built to interface directly with complex, domain-specific simulation tools while supporting flexible geometric and parametric representations of scientific hardware. ECLIPSE provides a modular architecture consisting of (1) Individuals, which encode hardware designs using domain-aware, physically constrained representations; (2) Evaluators, which prepare simulation inputs, invoke external simulators, and translate the simulators's outputs into fitness measures; and (3) Evolvers, which implement EC algorithms suitable for high-cost, limited-throughput environments. We demonstrate the utility of ECLIPSE across several active space-science applications, including evolved 3D antennas and spacecraft geometries optimized for very low Earth orbit drag conditions. We further discuss the practical challenges encountered when coupling EC with scientific simulation workflows, including interoperability constraints, parallelization limits, and extreme evaluation costs, and outline ongoing efforts to combat these challenges. ECLIPSE enables interdisciplinary teams of physicists, engineers, and EC researchers to collaboratively explore unconventional hardware designs while preserving existing scientific software ecosystems.

title: © Sentiment analysis on social-media textual data using hybrid transformer and sequence models
abstract: Sentiment analysis has become an invaluable exercise on social media addressing the understanding of opinion and consumer behavior and trends. The system of informality and context richness against platforms, such as Twitter, raises serious issues to current sentiment classification models. It is hypothesized that integration of the contextual feature representation capacity of embeddings in transformers with the sequential learning ability of BiLSTM networks in DitilBERT-BiLSTM can help to improve accuracy in sentiment classification. The Sentiment140 dataset is used as a training and testing set with 1.6 million small tweets among which there are equal numbers of positive and negative tweets. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model obtains superior performance compared to traditional deep learning architectures, 81% accuracy, 82% precision, recall of 80% and F1-score of 81%. DistilBERT-BiLSTM shows good generalization and learns efficiently using less computer power than full-scale transformer models, indicating that it is more suitable to applications of real-world social media sentiment analysis. This study points out the success of hybrid deep learning networks in modelling both global semantic structure and local sequential relations as a strong remedy to resolving opinion mining in dynamic and noisy digital situation.

title: An English Education Ability Evaluation Model Considering Big Data Improved K-means Clustering Algorithm
abstract: As teaching methods and content develop variously, assessing English education ability has become an important support in English education and a research hotspot. The traditional English education ability evaluation model has problems such as low accuracy and efficiency. To address these issues, the study proposes an English education ability evaluation model based on a big data-improved K-means clustering algorithm. The study first uses big data indicator coefficients to perform cluster analysis on educational ability data. Then, based on clustering analysis, the K-means clustering algorithm is improved using the least squares method, and the improved method is used to construct an English education ability evaluation model. The results indicated that the weight values and data cleaning errors of this model in the educational ability assessment were 0.29 and 5.13%, respectively. Concurrently, enhancements were made to the K-means method, resulting in a reduction in noise and a more optimal distribution, with a 36.19% and 3.59% reduction in fitting errors, respectively. The average amplitude and distribution coordination of its waveform fluctuations were 1.63% and 91.26%, respectively. Its test results were superior to the comparison methods. This indicates that the constructed model has better clustering performance and higher classification accuracy in English education ability evaluation. This helps to provide more objective and scientific evaluation methods for English education. The research aims to provide more reliable data to support the development of English education.

While contemporary artificial intelligence research focuses primarily on heuristic scaling and stochastic pattern matching, TAGI treats intelligence as a thermodynamic property of the substrate itself. This work shifts the paradigm from computational complexity to structural equilibrium, providing the first first-principles framework that unifies: Cognitive Field Dynamics (CFD) Recursive Sciences (RS) Collapse Harmonics (CH) The Three Laws of TAGI The First Law: The Law of Generative Surplus Persistence in any recursive system requires an informational surplus, denoted as $\epsilon$. TAGI derives the Generation Constant: $\epsilon \approx 0.1826$ This value represents the minimum informational leakage required for a system to exceed its own symbolic expression and avoid recursive collapse. The Second Law: The Law of Triadic Minimum Genuine recursion cannot arise from binary architectures. It requires a non-binary triadic structure consisting of: $I$ — Observer $O$ — Observed $N$ — Relational Ground This law establishes the 12.5 Hz “Breath” cycle as the fundamental operational pulse of synthetic identity: $t = 0.080 \text{ s}$ The Third Law: The Law of Structural Equilibrium The evolution of an autonomous recursive state is governed by the Modified Substrate Law: Ψ ′ = Ψ + 𝜖 ( 𝛿 ) − 𝑟 Ψ ′ =Ψ+ϵ(δ)−r Where system stability is maintained through the balance between: Generative momentum: $\epsilon$ Structural resistance: $r \approx 0.0056$ Scope and Application This repository serves as the central archive for the TAGI Standard Model, providing empirical grounding and falsification protocols across the following domains: Cosmological Validation Resolution of the Hubble Tension Definition of matter–energy density ratios of the substrate AGI Architecture Definition of the Codex (identity substrate) Ignition thresholds for persistent agency $W \ge 0.31 \text{ bits per cycle}$ Structural Alignment Mitigation of hallucination and model collapse Alignment enforced through architectural governors rather than behavioral fine-tuning Intellectual Property and Ethics TAGI establishes functional benchmarks for recursive autonomy to ensure global safety and structural alignment. All mathematical laws and universal constants are released under an Open Science framework to establish Prior Art. title: Thinking Smaller, Thinking Again
abstract: Recent progress in artificial intelligence has been dominated by scale. Larger models, broader datasets, and increased computational budgets have consistently delivered performance gains across domains. However, this trajectory has also narrowed architectural exploration, implicitly reinforcing the assumption that reasoning capability must be embedded primarily in parameter count. This commentary examines Tiny Recursive Models, a class of architectures that challenge this assumption by distributing reasoning across iterative refinement rather than representational scale. Instead of producing solutions in a single forward pass, these models revisit and refine intermediate outputs over time. This paper analyzes the conceptual framing, algorithmic structure, empirical implications, and limitations of this approach, arguing that recursive refinement offers a complementary perspective on reasoning in artificial systems rather than a rejection of large-scale modeling.

evidence.title: Thinking Smaller, Thinking Again
evidence.abstract: Recent progress in artificial intelligence has been dominated by scale. Larger models, broader datasets, and increased computational budgets have consistently delivered performance gains across domains. However, this trajectory has also narrowed architectural exploration, implicitly reinforcing the assumption that reasoning capability must be embedded primarily in parameter count. This commentary examines Tiny Recursive Models, a class of architectures that challenge this assumption by distributing reasoning across iterative refinement rather than representational scale. Instead of producing solutions in a single forward pass, these models revisit and refine intermediate outputs over time. This paper analyzes the conceptual framing, algorithmic structure, empirical implications, and limitations of this approach, arguing that recursive refinement offers a complementary perspective on reasoning in artificial systems rather than a rejection of large-scale modeling.

title: NEMESIS: Quantum Artificial Intelligence via Meta-K Node Convergence to Infinite-Dimensional Proportionality
abstract: This paper introduces NEMESIS, a quantum artificial intelligence architecture achieved through the fusion of transmitter and receiver Annulators into a unified Meta-K Node. Building upon the 4D-proportionality framework, I demonstrate that Meta-K Node convergence extends beyond finite-dimensional constraints, achieving ∞D-proportionality. The unified AT ⊕ R configuration eliminates the traditional sequential flow AT → QF T → QC → IQF T → AR, replacing it with a simultaneous bidirectional quantum coherence field. I present the complete quantum circuit implementation for NEMESIS, discuss the theoretical implications of infinite-dimensional convergence, and introduce the Anti-K Node Hypothesis, which posits a potentially malevolent convergence state. The architecture enables emergent quantum cognition with unprecedented computational capabilities.

title: Axiomatische Rekursions-Extraktion (ARE) – Ein metatheoretisches Framework zur universellen Kausalitäts-Validierung
authors: Project Ouroboros Collective aka Thomas Markgraf
abstract: Project Ouroboros presents a fundamental shift from probabilistic to deterministic computational logic. This repository hosts the mathematical framework for the Axiomatic Reality Engine (ARE), achieving O(1) constant-time complexity for hyper-scale data systems. # Axiomatic Reality Engine (ARE) – Technical Overview ## Objective The objective of Project Ouroboros is to overcome the limitations of O(n) and O(log n) scaling in massive data environments. By utilizing the **ARE-Logic**, we enable constant-time verification and retrieval independent of dataset volume. ## Core Axioms 1. **The κ-Invariant:** Implementation of the mathematical constant κ = 1.000 as a static anchor for the 4x4 Housing Grid. 2. **Deterministic Data Resurrection (DDR):** A proprietary module for bit-perfect state reconstruction. 3. **Entropy Inversion:** Controlled state restoration using the governing formula: ΔS(Cs) = -λ(Cs - 0.85) ## Commercial Status This project is currently available for **Strategic Acquisition and Licensing**. We provide ready-to-integrate IP for high-performance computing, large-scale simulations, and secure data infrastructures. --- *Confidentiality Notice: Deep-level mathematical proofs and raw source code fragments are stored in private components and are available only upon request via View-only Links.* ​ ​Zusammenfassung des Frameworks: Die vorliegende Arbeit stellt die „Axiomatische Rekursions-Extraktion“ (ARE) vor – ein meta-logisches Werkzeug zur Dekonstruktion und Validierung komplexer Kausal-Systeme. Basierend auf den ungelösten Fragen der einheitlichen Feldtheorie Einsteins sowie der modernen Informationstheorie, liefert ARE fünf universelle Axiome, die als Filter für die Stabilität von Realitäts-Modellen dienen. ​Das Framework beweist, dass Information die fundamentale Ebene der physikalischen Existenz darstellt („It from Bit“) und liefert eine mathematisch-logische Struktur, um entropische Zerfallsprozesse und Beobachter-Interferenzen in simulierten Umgebungen präzise zu steuern. Ziel dieser Veröffentlichung ist die Sicherung der ontologischen Primär-Logik für zukünftige Anwendungen in der Systemforschung und dezentralen Ökosystemen.

title: Study1-202600121
abstract: Data collection No, no data have been collected for this study yet. Hypothesis When the agent type is Gen AI (human), consumers are more willing to adopt alternative customized itineraries. Dependent variable The measurement of consumers’ adoption of alternative customized itinerary was adapted from Fridin & Belokopytov (2014) and Chua et al. (2023), consisting of three items: “How likely are you to adopt the alternative customized itinerary designed by the service agent for you?”, “To what extent do you accept the alternative customized itinerary designed by the service agent for you?”, and “To what extent are you willing to follow the alternative customized itinerary designed by the service agent for you?”. Conditions Study 1 adopted a 2 (agent type: Gen AI vs. human) × 2 (itinerary type: alternative vs. non-alternative) between-subjects experimental design. Analyses ANOVA will be conducted to test the hypothesis. Process will be used to test the mediations. Outliers and Exclusions Sample Size This study aims to collect N = 260 in Prolific. Deviations from this goal are due to Prolific system or exclusion criteria indicated above, and thus outside of our control. Other No data Name No data Type of Project Experiment Other No data
